pick.name: DaVinci Resolve
pick.what: Pro editor + colour + audio; free version plus one-time Studio licence
pick.why: Most powerful editor with a genuinely usable free version; Mac, Windows and Linux
pick.free_limits: Free: 8-bit formats to 60fps up to UHD; Studio $236 one-time (listed from $295; adds AI Neural Engine, text-based editing, 10-bit 120fps)

alts.name: CapCut
alts.what: Template-driven short-form editor with auto captions
alts.why: Fastest path to polished short-form clips
alts.free_limits: Free 1080p tier; Pro reported $19.99/mo or $179.99/yr (Oct 2026 secondary source; watermark rules conflict)
alts.maintained: Pricing page current; no Linux app

alts.name: Descript
alts.what: Edit video by editing the transcript
alts.why: Best for talking-head, podcast and demo content
alts.free_limits: Free: 1 media hr/mo, 720p, watermark, 100 one-time AI credits; Hobbyist $16/mo annual

candidates.name: DaVinci Resolve
candidates.verdict: PICK: best power and free tier

candidates.name: Final Cut Pro / Premiere Pro
candidates.verdict: Pro editors; not verified this pass (Final Cut is Apple-only)

candidates.name: Clipchamp
candidates.verdict: Free on Windows, 1080p no watermark (earlier pass)

decision: DaVinci Resolve is the best overall editor and its free version is enough for most founder videos. CapCut is faster for short-form and Descript for talking-head and demo videos edited by transcript.
details: CapCut free-tier watermark terms conflict across sources.

region_notes.India: CapCut is blocked in India; use Resolve, Clipchamp or Descript there.

os_notes.macOS: Resolve, CapCut, Descript or Final Cut Pro.
os_notes.Linux: Resolve and Kdenlive; CapCut and Descript have no Linux app.

verify.note: Verified: Resolve 21; Studio $236 (down from $295); free capped at 8-bit, 60 fps, UHD.
